attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Medical cover for the Tanners Row Community Run Half Marathon, Sunday 1 August 2027

In recent years the last runner has usually finished well inside the time limit, and past incidents have been limited to a few blisters and one twisted ankle. A number of members have first aid certificates from work and are glad to be there in a general helping role.

From Carl Jensen, Event Secretary, Tanners Row Business Association

The race is a half marathon with 100 runners and starts at 10:00. We expect a crew from St. Luke Ambulance Brigade on the day, though we have nothing in writing yet.

First aid
We'll have 3 first aid posts, at the start, the finish and halfway, with 6 trained first aiders between them, so nobody on the course is more than about a kilometre and a half from help. We also have two first aiders on bikes, carrying defibrillators.

Heat, cold and water
There's water every 2.5 km. We look at the forecast two days before and again two hours before. Over 28 degrees we start earlier or cut the course, and over 32 degrees we call it off. If it's cold or wet, we have foil blankets and a warm tent at the finish.

If someone needs hospital
The nearest emergency department is at Thornton County Hospital, 18 km from the finish. We've walked the route out from the pick-up point at the top of Copper Row with the first aiders, and we've told the hospital the date and how many are coming.

Staying in touch
Everyone at a post and both bike first aiders has a radio on our medical channel, with phones as backup. Calls for an ambulance go through our medical lead, who tells the crew which barrier to come to.

Who's responsible
Our medical lead is Grace Lindqvist, a registered paramedic, who'll be there from an hour before the start until the last runner is in and has the final word on pulling any runner out.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Tanners Row Community Run Half Marathon: how the race will work

Prepared by Carl Jensen (Event Secretary), Tanners Row Business Association. Last updated 31 May 2027.

This is our plan for race day, Sunday 1 August 2027. We expect 100 runners over half marathon (21 km). Numbers can be collected from the top of Copper Row from an hour before we go at 10:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 13:30.

The route takes in Copper Row, Glebe Road, Tanner Street and Garrison Street, and the City would need to close all of these for us. On the way round we cross Ferry Road and High Street. We finish in Ferry Park lawn.

Anyone who knows the area will know these are old streets. Copper Row is only about 5 metres wall to wall, Tanner Street is around 5.5 metres once you allow for parked vans we can't move, and Garrison Street is about 5 metres. We line everyone up along Copper Row because there's nowhere else to put them. The last stretch has shopfronts tight on both sides.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Tanners Row Community Run Half Marathon
Date: Sunday 1 August 2027
Applicant: Tanners Row Business Association
Prepared by: Corvus Temporary Works
Issue: 3.1

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Tanners Row Community Run Half Marathon, a half marathon race in the Eastfield area of Port Halden with a 10:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. Police attendance is covered in the attached correspondence.

2. Road closures
The principal closure will be on Copper Row. Elsewhere on the course, traffic will be held dynamically by the appointed contractor as the field passes, in line with accepted industry practice. Pathfinder Road Crews will confirm the detailed arrangements following a pre-event site visit.

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 08:30 until the last runner has passed.
- Ferry Road at Tanner Street: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- High Street at Garrison Street: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Drivers will be advised to expect delays in the area and to allow additional time for their journeys. Advance information boards will be used where practical, and through traffic is expected to find alternative routes across the wider network.

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
Details of the event will be published on the organiser's website and shared through social media in the weeks leading up to race day.

We have a good working relationship with local residents. Several members walk the route the week before, noting anything that has changed, such as new roadworks, a barrier left in place, or a lane marked for cycles.

7. Reopening
A sweep vehicle follows the last runner. Closures are lifted in the order listed, after a barrier and litter check, with all roads open by 14:00.
